Running on a cluster

Source: vignettes/Clusters.Rmd
Clusters.Rmd

On a computing cluster, RiboPilot sends each step of the pipeline to the cluster’s scheduler as a job, and runs the analysis tools in Singularity (or Apptainer). You still use the app to review results and export.

Choose a profile

A profile tells RiboPilot/Nextflow how to submit jobs on your cluster. Two are built in and ready to use: executor = "NMNH_Hydra" and executor = "NOAA_SEDNA". Each has its own setup page: Smithsonian Hydra setup and NOAA SEDNA setup.

For any other Slurm, SGE, PBS, or LSF cluster, make a Nextflow profile once with RiboPilot::generate_config(), then pass its name to new_project():

RiboPilot::generate_config(
  "mylab_slurm",
  scheduler       = "slurm",
  queue           = "general",
  account         = "mylab",
  walltime        = "48h",
  container_cache = "/scratch/mylab/singularity"
)
RiboPilot::new_project(path = "/shared/mylab/my_project",
  mapping_fn = "/shared/mylab/my_samples.csv",
  data_path = "/shared/mylab/reads", 
  executor = "mylab_slurm")

container_cache is the folder where Singularity keeps the RiboPilot image, shared by every project that uses the profile. If you leave it out, RiboPilot uses NXF_SINGULARITY_CACHEDIR when that is set, and otherwise a containers folder inside your reference folder. Many clusters need a walltime: some reject a job that asks for none.

Profiles are saved in your own settings folder (on Linux, ~/.config/R/RiboPilot). To share one with your lab, save it in a shared folder with profile_dir, and pass the same profile_dir to new_project():

RiboPilot::generate_config(
  "mylab_slurm",
  scheduler   = "slurm",
  queue       = "general",
  walltime    = "48h",
  profile_dir = "/shared/mylab/ribopilot_profiles"
)
RiboPilot::new_project(
  path        = "/shared/mylab/my_project",
  mapping_fn  = "/shared/mylab/my_samples.csv",
  data_path   = "/shared/mylab/reads",
  executor    = "mylab_slurm",
  profile_dir = "/shared/mylab/ribopilot_profiles"
)

Manual profile edits. You can manually adjust profiles in the profile_dir. This may be necessary for clusters that use a customized job scheduler. If you are unsure how to do this, please consult your cluster’s job submission documentation or contact a cluster admin. For additional guidance, check NF-core to see if your cluster already has a custom config or instructions.

Put everything on shared storage

The project folder, the reads, the reference folder, and the R library that holds RiboPilot must be visible from the login node and from every compute node.

Open the app

On RStudio Server, just run RiboPilot::RiboPilot("/shared/mylab/my_project").

Without RStudio Server, run R and start the app on the login node or an interactive session to reach it from your own computer through an SSH tunnel:

RiboPilot::RiboPilot("/shared/mylab/my_project", port = 8123,
                     launch.browser = FALSE)

The app prints the address to open and the tunnel command. On your own computer, in a terminal:

ssh -N -L 8123:localhost:8123 you@login.cluster.edu

Then open http://localhost:8123 in your browser.

When a batch scheduler (sbatch, qsub, or bsub) is on the PATH, or the app runs on RStudio Server, the run window offers a job script to submit instead of Run from App. The headless argument of RiboPilot() overrides this:

# Always offer a job script, even when no scheduler is detected
RiboPilot::RiboPilot("/shared/mylab/my_project", headless = TRUE)

# Always offer Run from App: Nextflow runs inside the R session that
# started the app, not through the scheduler
RiboPilot::RiboPilot("/shared/mylab/my_project", headless = FALSE)

headless = FALSE only makes sense when the machine running R is allowed to do the work itself, for example an interactive compute session. Most clusters forbid heavy jobs on login nodes.

Submit a run as a job

Press Update. The run window shows the job script for the Nextflow head job. The head job is small but long-lived: 2 CPUs, 8 GB of memory, and 48 hours, in the queue and with the account from your profile. Check the partition, account, walltime, and memory, and edit the script in the window if you need to. Then press Submit as job, or Save script to submit it yourself.

The job runs on its own, so you can close the browser and watch the job with your scheduler’s tools (e.g. qstat on Hydra). Once job is done, use the reload button above the table to see new results. The app does not track a submitted job, so do not start another run for the same project until the job has finished.

Each submission leaves three kinds of files in the project’s .runs folder:

  • .runs/jobs/: the job scripts;
  • .runs/logs/: the scheduler’s log for each job;
  • .runs/nextflow/: one Nextflow log per run.

Once a job has finished, use Run Reports in the toolbar to see how it went.

In the Assemble step, Work Dirs finds the pipeline’s working folders for a sample, from both app runs and cluster jobs.
